sections.h2: Who records deeds in Clarion County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
The Clarion County Register and Recorder's Office records them. It occupies Suite 24 of the courthouse at 421 Main Street in the borough of Clarion, and callers reach it at (814) 226-4000. One elected officer, serving a four-year term, runs the whole office, which also handles wills, estates and Orphans' Court filings.

The Recorder of Deeds side of the office files land documents, veterans' discharges, notary bonds and commissions, and powers of attorney. Its land records run back to 1840, and the office also holds a small number of deeds from Venango and Armstrong counties dating to 1800, the two counties Clarion County was carved from.

Anyone may look through the records on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30. Staff cannot give legal advice, so a seller with a title question goes to a lawyer or the closing agent, not the counter clerk.

For anyone selling a house in Clarion County, this office is the last stop. Once the deed is signed at closing, it is recorded here, and the recording is what puts the buyer's name in the public record.

sections.h2: What should I expect to pay the Clarion County recorder?
sections.html:
Ask the Register and Recorder's Office for the current Recorder of Deeds fee schedule before closing day. The county keeps a fee schedule page under its Register and Recorder section, and a deed's cost depends on its page count and the number of names indexed, so the title agent should confirm the total in advance.

How you pay matters as much as how much. The office stopped accepting credit and debit cards on June 1, 2025, which means a closing package should arrive with a check for the recording fee and a check for the transfer tax. If the title company handles recording for you, ask which of its checks covers each charge.

  • Bring checks, because cards have been refused at this counter since June 1, 2025.
  • Count the pages and the names on the deed, since both can raise the recording fee.
  • Ask whether the office can accept the package by mail and whether a return envelope is needed.
  • Keep the recording receipt; it shows the date the new owner entered the record.

sections.h2: How is realty transfer tax handled when a Clarion County house sells?
sections.html:
The state tax is one percent of what the property is worth, and it is collected at recording by the county recorder. Under the state's rules the grantor and the grantee are both held jointly and severally liable, so a missed payment can be pursued against either party.

Counties usually collect an additional local realty transfer tax at the same time. The recorder forwards the 1 percent state share to the Department of Revenue, and local governments may split their share between the school district and the municipality. For a Clarion County sale, ask the recorder which local rate applies to the borough or township where the house stands.

Some transfers are exempt from the tax, and the state lists them.

  • Certain transfers among family members.
  • Transfers to governmental units and between religious organizations.
  • Transfers to shareholders or partners, and to or from nonprofit industrial development agencies.
  • Deeds to burial sites and farms, and property passed by will or intestate succession.

Anyone claiming an exemption should ask the recorder what paperwork the office wants to see with the deed.

sections.h2: How do I search Clarion County land records?
sections.html:
Many records can be searched online around the clock through the Infocon County Access System, a subscription service that the county points people to. Searching in person is free during public hours, and the office keeps land records from 1840 forward.

An online search helps a seller in a few ways. It shows whether an older mortgage was ever satisfied of record, whether a prior deed in the chain was recorded, and what the legal description looked like when the current owner bought. An heir who inherited a Clarion County house can also check how the previous owner took title. Birth and death certificates after 1906 are not kept here; those are filed with the state's vital records office, and the county page links to VitalChek for ordering.

Military discharge papers and adoption records are the exceptions to the public-access rule, so an owner who needs a veteran's discharge on file should ask the office how to request it.

sections.h2: What is the Clarion County setting like?
sections.html:
Clarion County covers 610 square miles of Northwestern Pennsylvania, with 601 of them land. The county seat is the borough of Clarion, which had 3,931 residents in 2020, and the county courthouse stands there. PennWest Clarion is the university in the county. Other boroughs include Knox, New Bethlehem, Rimersburg, East Brady, Sligo, Strattanville and Shippenville.

The county was erected on March 11, 1839 from parts of Venango and Armstrong counties and is named for the Clarion River, which runs through its middle. Lumber moved down that river first, iron followed, and oil drilling spread through the area after the 1859 oil strike in northwestern Pennsylvania. Part of Cook Forest State Park lies inside the county, and I-80, US 322 and PA 66 are among the highways that cross it.

The Census Bureau counted 36,680 residents in July 2025, 1.5 percent fewer than the count after the 2020 census. Winters are cold; the average January temperature in Clarion borough is about 24.5 degrees Fahrenheit, which matters to a buyer asking about a furnace, a roof and a chimney.

sections.h2: What should I check before a Clarion County closing?
sections.html:
A short list prevents a delay at the recorder's counter.

  • Phone (814) 226-4000 to confirm the current fee schedule and any recording requirements for the deed.
  • Make sure the deed names the municipality where the property sits, since the local transfer tax follows that location.
  • Prepare checks for the recording fee and for state and local transfer tax; the office stopped taking cards on June 1, 2025.
  • If a family exemption or another exemption applies, ask what form the office needs filed with the deed.
  • Decide who will deliver the package and who receives the recorded original.

Sellers who need to sell quickly, such as heirs or owners behind on payments, can still work through the same recording steps. Cash buyers still sign a deed, the deed is still recorded in Clarion, and the transfer tax is still calculated on the sale price.

faqs.q: Where do I take a deed in Clarion County?
faqs.a: Go to the Register and Recorder's Office in the Clarion County Courthouse, Suite 24, 421 Main Street, Clarion, PA 16214. The phone number is (814) 226-4000, and the public may inspect records on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30.

faqs.q: Will the Clarion County office take a debit card?
faqs.a: No. The office stopped accepting credit and debit card payments on June 1, 2025, so bring a check for the recording fee and for the transfer tax.

faqs.q: What does Pennsylvania charge when a house changes hands?
faqs.a: The state tax is one percent of what the property is worth, and buyer and seller are both liable under the Department of Revenue's description. Counties usually collect a local tax of their own at recording, so the total is higher than 1 percent.

faqs.q: How old are the land records held in Clarion?
faqs.a: Land records run back to 1840 in the county's own description, and the office also holds a few deeds from Venango and Armstrong counties dating to 1800. Many of the records can be searched online through a subscription service.

faqs.q: Does Clarion County require an attorney at the recorder's counter?
faqs.a: The recorder's office does not give legal advice, so a lawyer or the closing agent should prepare the deed and answer questions about exemptions. The office itself records the document once it meets its requirements and the fees are paid.
